questions.question: What makes content_vector("hello", dim=64) repeatable?
options: It uses the current microphone waveform
It samples a new random vector on every call
It hashes the text with SHA-256 and deterministically maps bytes to values
It looks up a speaker name in the leaderboard
questions.explanation: The SHA-256 digest is expanded to the requested dimension, so the same text gives the same vector.

questions.question: What does speaker_vector(seed, dim=64) normalize?
options: The payload bits to a probability distribution
The input text to lowercase
The audio sample rate to 16 kHz
A seeded Gaussian vector to unit L2 norm
questions.explanation: It draws Gaussian values with random.Random(seed), then divides by their Euclidean norm.

questions.question: With mix=0.5, how does fake_tts combine content c and speaker s?
options: 0.5*c + 0.5*s element by element
c+s without scaling
c-s followed by softmax
Only the speaker vector, discarding content
questions.explanation: The expression is (1-mix)*c + mix*s for each paired coordinate.

questions.question: How does extract_speaker choose a reference speaker?
options: The first name alphabetically
The name with the highest cosine similarity to the generated vector
The speaker with the longest reference vector
The name encoded in the text content
questions.explanation: It computes cosine against every reference vector, sorts descending, and returns the first pair.

questions.question: What does detect_watermark estimate from wave_original and wave_wm?
options: The exact original text using SHA-256 inversion
The speaker identity from the waveform spectrum
Each bit from the sign of the average watermark difference at its stride positions
The sample rate from the WAV header
questions.explanation: It forms wave_wm-wave_original, averages positions b::n_bits, and emits one when the average is positive.

questions.question: Why does the toy voice-conversion step preserve content while changing speaker?
options: It drops all content and generates silence
It copies Bob’s waveform unchanged and renames the file
It changes only the sample rate, which changes identity
It extracts a content vector from Bob’s utterance and resynthesizes it with Alice’s speaker vector
questions.explanation: The pipeline separates the two representations, then calls fake_tts with the recovered content and target speaker embedding.
